## Registration date / business-day adjustment

### 1. Class implementing the business-day / date-adjustment logic

**`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/function/owner/ResolveRegistrationDate.java`** — this is the class that performs the weekend roll-forward adjustment. The core logic is at **lines 26-34** (`service` method), with the weekend-skip loop at **lines 29-32**.

This is an OfficeFloor "function" step in the `POST /api/owners` flow (not a Spring `@Service`). It resolves the effective date (supplied-or-`LocalDate.now()`) and rolls Saturday/Sunday forward one day at a time until a weekday is reached, then publishes it as an `Out<LocalDate>` variable consumed by later steps.

### 2. Full source of the relevant method

From `ResolveRegistrationDate.java`:
```java
public void service(@Val OwnerFieldsDto request, Out<LocalDate> registrationDate) {
    LocalDate effective = request.getRegistrationDate() != null
            ? request.getRegistrationDate() : LocalDate.now();
    while (effective.getDayOfWeek() == DayOfWeek.SATURDAY
            || effective.getDayOfWeek() == DayOfWeek.SUNDAY) {
        effective = effective.plusDays(1);
    }
    registrationDate.set(effective);
}
```

Two closely related steps in the same package:
- **`DefaultOwnerRegistrationDate.java`** (lines 17-19) — applies the single resolved/adjusted `LocalDate` to the `Owner` entity (`owner.setRegistrationDate(registrationDate)`), overwriting any raw weekend date from the request.
- **`ValidateRegistrationDate.java`** (lines 20-29) — runs before resolution; rejects a *supplied* future date (`supplied.isAfter(LocalDate.now())`) via `FutureRegistrationDateException`. Does not do weekend adjustment.

### 3. Related test files

**`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/acceptance/AcceptanceTest.java`** — test method `coreDefaultDateIsBusinessDay()` (lines 14-19). It is a black-box acceptance test: it creates an owner and asserts the returned `registrationDate` `DayOfWeek` is neither `SATURDAY` nor `SUNDAY`.

Helper methods used by the test live in **`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/acceptance/AcceptanceBase.java`**: `structuredOwner()` (line 136), `createOwnerOk(...)` (line 160), `fetchOwner(int id)` (line 200).

I found no unit test that directly instantiates `ResolveRegistrationDate` — coverage is only via this acceptance test.

### 4. How dates/holidays are represented

- Dates use `java.time.LocalDate` throughout: the `Owner` entity field (`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/model/Owner.java`, line 67 `private LocalDate registrationDate;`, getter/setter lines 163-168), the DTO (`OwnerFieldsDto.getRegistrationDate()`), and all three function steps.
- Weekday detection uses `java.time.DayOfWeek` (`DayOfWeek.SATURDAY` / `DayOfWeek.SUNDAY`).
- Serialized as ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` (noted in the `DefaultOwnerRegistrationDate` Javadoc; the test parses it with `LocalDate.parse(...)`).

### Note on "public holidays"
The `AcceptanceTest` Javadoc (lines 9-11) claims the default date "rolls past public holidays as well as weekends," but **no holiday calendar is actually implemented** — a `grep` for `holiday`/`calendar` across `src/main` returns nothing, and `ResolveRegistrationDate` only skips Saturday/Sunday. So the code currently adjusts for weekends only; the holiday claim in the test comment is aspirational/unimplemented (the test deliberately asserts only the weaker weekend invariant).

The change is implemented and the full test suite is green (BUILD SUCCESS, 1 test run, 0 failures).

## What I did

The business-day roll-forward for the registration date lived in one place: `ResolveRegistrationDate.service(...)`, which was skipping only Saturdays and Sundays. I extended it to also roll past the fixed public holidays.

`src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/function/owner/ResolveRegistrationDate.java`:
- Added a `Set<LocalDate> PUBLIC_HOLIDAYS` containing 2026-01-01, 2026-01-26, 2026-04-25, 2026-12-25, 2026-12-28.
- Extended the existing roll-forward loop so it advances one day whenever the date is a Saturday, Sunday, **or** a listed holiday — repeating until it reaches a non-holiday weekday. This naturally chains (e.g. a holiday that lands next to a weekend keeps rolling), and it keeps the single-source-of-truth guarantee the class already provides (daily create-limit, stored date, and membership-number year all derive from this one adjusted date).
- Updated the Javadoc to mention public holidays.

Because the resolved date is published once as `Out<LocalDate>` and consumed downstream by `@Val`, no other step needed changing.
